observations: Industrial sewing machine mounted on a dedicated power table.
Brand 'EMEL' is visible on the machine head and the table surface.
Large clutch-style motor mounted under the table.
Thread stand with four spool pins and thread guides.
Foot pedal and knee lifter are present.
A green manual grommet or button press is on the floor nearby.
The machine is threaded and appears to be in an active workspace.

claims.evidence: The model number is not legible on the machine head or plate in the provided photos.
No manufacturing plate is visible to confirm the country of origin; EMEL is typically associated with Chinese manufacturing.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual
claims.evidence: Manual and accessories are not shown in any of the photos.

claims.claim: never serviced because nothing ever went wrong

risks.risk: The motor may be burnt out or excessively noisy.
risks.proof: A video clip of the motor starting and the machine stitching.

risks.risk: The machine may be a standard Chinese model rather than the claimed Japanese origin.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the metal specification plate on the back or side of the machine head.

risks.risk: Internal timing or tension issues hidden by static photos.
risks.proof: A photo of a 'sew-off' (a sample of stitching on fabric) performed by this machine.

proof_requests: Photo of the metal identification plate on the machine head showing the model number and country of manufacture.
A video of the machine running and stitching through fabric.
Photo of the manual and included accessories.

response.reason: The brand is confirmed as EMEL, but the specific model and the high-value claim of being 'Japanese made' cannot be verified without a clear shot of the identification plate. The presence of the manual and accessories is also unproven.
